preamble: Raising of the first element of the diphthong [oi] to [ui] is attested in Latin, where Old Latin dative quoi (also quoei, quoiei) became Classical Latin cui. The raising follows the labiovelar, as in quom > cum and quoius > cuius. Latin generally monophthongized oi (via oe to ū, as in oinos > ūnus), so cui is a relic in which the diphthong survived with a raised nucleus.

examples.from: Old Latin quoi, quoiei (< Proto-Italic *kʷojjei) 'to whom'
examples.note: Dative singular of the relative quī and interrogative quis.
